turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he would call Estella right away, ma’am, and left to do so with a sense of both dread and curiosity.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched as Pip left the room, her eyes following him with a mix of curiosity and a darker, more sinister purpose. She wondered how Estella would fare in her absence, and how Pip might react to the young woman’s company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip knocked gently at the door and called out Estella’s name, his voice barely above a whisper, feeling both the weight of Miss Havisham’s request and the looming presence of the unknown Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the door intently, her eyes narrowing as she waited for Estella to appear. She wondered how the boy would react to Estella’s presence and if she might find in Pip a new pawn in her twisted game.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip waited nervously as Estella appeared, her presence both intriguing and intimidating. He stepped aside to let her pass, his eyes fixed on the ground, and followed her back to Miss Havisham's room.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She observed the two children entering the room, her gaze piercing and unyielding, as if searching for something hidden within their youthful innocence.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his heart pounding in his chest as he entered the room, his eyes darting nervously around, and he shuffled his feet as he followed Estella, keeping a respectful distance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She motioned for Pip to approach, her eyes never leaving him as she commanded, Estella, fetch the boy a seat.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip watched Miss Havisham and felt a surge of nervousness, his feet shuffling as he hesitantly approached a chair.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She stared at Pip with an intensity that made the boy shift uncomfortably, as if trying to discern some hidden truth within his young, unblemished soul.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He felt a shiver run down his spine as he sat down, his eyes fixed on Miss Havisham, who seemed to be studying him like an insect under a microscope.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She watched him closely, her eyes narrowing as if she were trying to see through his youthful innocence to the man he would one day become.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He felt like a stranger in a dream, his nerves on edge as he stammered out that he did not understand why he was there, please, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham let out a sigh, her eyes never leaving Pip's as she spoke in a tone that was both commanding and enigmatic. She told him that understanding was not necessary at this moment, but to simply be present, to let her gaze pierce through his youthful facade.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt Miss Havisham's gaze like a weight on his chest, and he nodded, his voice barely above a whisper, telling her that he would try to be present as she wished.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham leaned forward, her eyes still locked with Pip's, and with a voice that seemed to carry the weight of a hundred unspoken words, she told him that he would learn to understand in time, but for now, he was to observe, to absorb.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He nodded again, feeling a strange mix of fear and curiosity, telling Miss Havisham he would try to understand as she wished.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham leaned back, her gaze softening slightly, and with a voice that hinted at a world of secrets, told Pip that he would be shown things that were not meant for his eyes, but that he would come to see the truth in them.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a shiver run down his spine, and he murmured that he would do as Miss Havisham asked, though he did not understand what truths he would see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes glinted with a mixture of curiosity and something darker, telling Pip that the world was full of lessons one learned in the harshest of ways, and that his time here would be no different.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
